title: iEEG during direct electrical stimulation of orbitofrontal and other sites (Rao, Sellers et al., 2018): continuous-stimulation and single-pulse recordings
description: Intracranial EEG (ECoG grids/strips and depth/stereo-EEG electrodes) from 17 adults undergoing inpatient seizure monitoring, recorded before, during and after direct electrical stimulation of the lateral orbitofrontal cortex and other sites. The dataset includes continuous 100 Hz stimulation and single-pulse stimulation recordings, along with mood and depression assessments. The associated study found that unilateral lateral OFC stimulation acutely improved mood in participants with moderate-to-severe baseline depression symptoms.
methods_description: Recordings were made with Natus clinical, Tucker-Davis Technologies, or Alpha Omega NeuroOmega systems at 1-25 kHz. Continuous bipolar stimulation (1 or 6 mA, 100 Hz, 100 us pulse width, 100-200 s) was delivered with a Nicolet Cortical Stimulator, with a sham block at the start of each session. Mood was assessed with the tablet-based Immediate Mood Scaler and verbal reports. Single-pulse stimulation used 10 mA, 1 Hz, 500 us pulses.
